{"claims":[{"claim_text":"The U.S. government is neglecting the fate of the people of Puerto Rico when it suits the interests of powerful, wealthy bondholders who own Puerto Rico’s debt obligations.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Alejandro Garcia Padilla contends that Puerto Rico must be able to renegotiate payment on its roughly $72 billion in debts to pull the island out of a “death spiral”.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Democratic Socialists of America calls on all political parties in Puerto Rico, the U.S. Congress, and the Obama Administration to join together to develop a long-term plan that addresses the root causes of the crisis.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"The U.S. government should provide economic aid to help restructure Puerto Rico’s government and public corporate debt so as to lower its debt burden and the costs of repayment.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[3]},{"claim_text":"Refusing to consider policies to provide economic aid will guarantee severe austerity programs and brutal cuts in ordinary people’s living standards.",
"claim_types":["prediction"],"evidence_ids":[3]},{"claim_text":"Lowering the quality of life for ordinary Puerto Ricans aims to ensure that the wealthy holders of Puerto Rican debt are repaid.",
"claim_types":["evaluation"],"evidence_ids":[3]},{"claim_text":"The repayment crisis is in large part due to a long-term economic crisis caused by corporate disinvestment from the island.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[3]},{"claim_text":"The costs of restoring economic health to the island should be borne primarily by those who continued to profit during the crisis.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[3]}],"unresolved_references":[]}
